heroLede: Exhibition-making, moving image and the records we keep. A practice built on the material of ordinary life.
heroImageAlt: Abstract exhibition graphic in charcoal, light grey and black
heroCaptionLeft: Home Affairs: The Everyday is the Archive
practiceHeading: Azola Krweqe is an artist and curator whose work moves between exhibition-making, moving image and research.
practiceBody:
Her practice begins with what is already there — family photographs, public records, the objects people keep — and asks how those materials shape the stories we tell about ourselves. Projects are built slowly, through conversation, and often take the form of a room to be entered rather than a statement to be read.

Recent work brings artists and makers together around the archive as a living room rather than a locked cabinet: something entered, rearranged and returned to.
projectsHeading: Work that begins with what is already there.
writingHeading: Notes on images, archives and display.
